subject.title: fix(mcp): standalone apps stop hanging on stalled gateway requests

question: Should a session MCP runtime continue an already-started catalog refresh after its last App-operation waiter times out, so the shared cache can still be warmed, or should it abort that refresh when no callers remain?
rationale: Both policies are technically plausible, but they impose different shared-resource and latency semantics; the repository needs an owner decision rather than an automated preference.

options.title: Keep runtime-owned refreshes
options.body: Accept continuation after caller detachment, with only catalog invalidation and runtime disposal aborting the generation, to retain shared-cache warming and session reuse.

options.title: Abort orphaned refreshes
options.body: Cancel a current catalog generation once its final operation waiter detaches, trading potential cache warming for tighter resource reclamation.

recommendation.title: Keep runtime-owned refreshes
recommendation.body: Accept continuation after caller detachment, with only catalog invalidation and runtime disposal aborting the generation, to retain shared-cache warming and session reuse.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied outside reviewer specifically says this ownership decision needs an MCP runtime owner, while no dependable current-main owner provenance was available to identify a person.
